problem.summary: Three witness workflows carried freshness/latency SLO targets below their own observed steady-state inter-run gap, producing permanent false freshness_miss/latency_miss findings while the witnesses were in fact firing normally.
problem.root_cause: GitHub hosted cron does not fire every scheduled slot for sub-daily crons. Observed over 5+ days, one slot per day is consistently dropped on each of these workflows, so the real inter-run gap ceiling is well above the nominal cron cadence. Targets had been pinned near cadence (4-6% margin), so the miss was structural, not incidental.
problem.prior_false_alarm_history: Same alert class previously re-pinned in PR #104; these three entries were not covered.

evidence.method: GitHub Actions scheduled-run history (event=schedule) read via gh run list; gaps computed between consecutive fires.

workflows.pattern: repeating 6-fire daily cycle with one dropped slot: 173/231/233/200/227/376
workflows.target_vs_double_cadence: 420 < 480, two consecutive genuine misses still trip

non_weakening_argument.claim: This is a detector correction, not a test weakening.
reasons: Every new target remains strictly below 2x the nominal cron cadence, so a genuinely stopped loop (two consecutive missed fires) still trips the SLO.
Every new target is set from the measured steady-state maximum gap plus a small headroom, not from a desired-green value.
The prior targets could not be satisfied by a healthy system, so they carried zero detection signal and desensitized the critique surface.

not_touched: daily witnesses (motor_sustain, sourcea_spine, stack_health) — measured gaps ~1440 min against 1560 targets, stable, left unchanged
weekly witnesses (autorun, gha_health, machine_audit) — not flagging, left unchanged
success_rate targets and all non-SLO registry fields
